text:
maya: Heads-up — planning a small change to the gateway rewrite engine to support canary routing and safer header stripping. Idea: inject X-Client-Version for canary routing, remove sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) early, and allow an opt-in query param override but with lower precedence than explicit header. Does that align with previous assumptions about routing precedence?

devon: Are we injecting X-Client-Version from the console rollout selector or deriving from client headers?

maya: Console will set it for canary rollouts. For client-sent values we want to preserve them but not let them trump the console flag. So rewrite precedence is: route-level overrides (console) > client headers > fallback.

alex: +1 for header injection. Note: query param overrides break CDN caching more often. If we must support query overrides, they should be sanitized and normalized (single value, no repeated params). Also prefer header-based routing for performance.

jordan: Also watch signed-url flows (S3, downloads) — removing or normalizing query params can break them. We should keep a path allowlist or regex patterns where we skip query rewrites.

devon: Proposed rule set (pseudo-YAML):

```yaml
route_rewrites:
  - route: /api/v1/preview/*
    remove_headers: [Authorization, Cookie]   # strip auth before routing to internal services
    inject_headers:
      X-Client-Version: route.override.version  # set by console when rollouts active
    query_handling:
      merge_strategy: client-first
      allowlist_paths: ["/download/*", "/s3-presigned/*"]
      normalize: true  # collapse repeated params, percent-decode normalization

# precedence: route override > header > client query param > server default
```

sre-bot: config-lint: query_normalization rule flagged on 1 route (possible allowlist miss). See lint report: https://ci.internal.redwood/reports/1245

maya: Good catch. We'll make the allowlist configurable and default to conservative (no rewrites on paths that look like presigned URLs). Also add logging/audit of original request when we rewrite so we can debug breakages quickly.

alex: Test cases to add: (1) client sends ?debug=true + console X-Client-Version header -> console header wins, backend sees no debug param unless whitelisted. (2) repeated params: a=1&a=2 -> normalized to a=1 (or last?) decide on rule. I prefer last wins for compatibility with how many frameworks parse.

jordan: For the repeated param rule, prefer 'last wins' is fine but call it out in docs and in telemetry. Also ensure no change for application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies.

devon: I'll draft a PR with a feature flag `gateway.rewrites.v2` and a console toggle per-routing-rule. Assigning @maya for UX and @alex for test coverage.

maya: SG. Can we also emit a metric `gateway.rewrite.apply.{route}.{type}` (eg. header_inject, header_strip, query_normalize) so we can monitor how often rewrites fire and detect cache-busting spikes?

jordan: +1. Add an alert on rewrite.apply rate increase > 3x baseline that ties to cache-miss rate in CDN.

devon: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/812 (WIP) — includes the proto and a small Envoy filter stub. pinging eng-sre for canary.

sre-bot: deploy-check: lint OK, integration: pending (will run on canary).

maya: Thanks everyone. If eng-sre flags anything about CDN caching we should pause the console rollout. Schedule a 15m sync if needed. :thumbsup:
